items.question: What ritual means certainly bring brahmins under control?
premises: Flowers born from girikarṇī are used as oblation material.
The ritual act aims at subjugation.
The result is declared certain.
items.inference: Offering flowers born from girikarṇī certainly subjugates brahmins.
items.plain_english: One should certainly subjugate brahmins with flowers born from girikarṇī.

rows.grounds: targets, sons of previously mentioned brahmins

items.question: How can the sons of those brahmins be brought under control?
premises: Mālatī flowers are offered in oblation.
The sons of the brahmins are the intended targets.
The ritual aims to bring them under control.
items.inference: By offering mālatī flowers, one brings their sons under control.
items.plain_english: Having offered mālatī flowers, one should bring their sons under control.

items.question: What oblation material can instantly subjugate kings?
premises: Mustard seeds mixed with pungent substances are used.
Kings are the intended targets.
The effect occurs instantly.
items.inference: Offering pungent-mixed mustard seeds instantly subjugates kings.
items.plain_english: One should subjugate kings in an instant with mustard seeds mixed with pungent substances.

items.question: Can oblation certainly subjugate men, women, and kings together?
premises: Men, women, and kings are named as targets.
Oblation is the means employed.
The result is declared certain.
items.inference: By oblation one certainly subjugates men, women, and kings.
items.plain_english: By oblation one should certainly subjugate men, women, and kings.

rows.grounds: indicates result occurs before a year passes

items.question: What status does the practitioner attain within a year through this practice?
premises: The result arises before a year passes.
Fortune accompanies the practitioner.
Kings are conquered.
items.inference: Within a year the practitioner becomes fortunate and conquers kings.
items.plain_english: Within a year he becomes one who has conquered kings through fortune.

items.question: What degree of beauty does the practitioner immediately attain?
premises: Beauty is attained immediately.
Kandarpa is the point of comparison.
The attained beauty exceeds that standard.
items.inference: The practitioner immediately attains beauty greater than Kandarpa’s.
items.plain_english: He immediately attains beauty greater than that of Kandarpa.

items.question: What lifespan follows from conquering all diseases through this practice?
premises: All diseases are conquered.
The practitioner is the subject of the result.
A lifespan of a hundred autumns is stated.
items.inference: Having conquered all diseases, he should live a hundred years.
items.plain_english: Having conquered all diseases, he should live for a hundred years.

items.question: Who becomes submissive to the practitioner through mutual contact?
premises: The practitioner may touch others or be touched by them.
Contact creates a relation of influence.
The effect occurs soon.
items.inference: Those whom he touches or who touch him soon become submissive to him.
items.plain_english: Those whom he touches, or by whom he is touched, should soon become submissive to him.

items.question: Is mere sight sufficient for subjugation without further deliberation?
premises: Subjugation occurs by sight alone.
The verse denies the need for consideration.
The claim is presented as certain.
items.inference: One subjugates by sight alone, and no deliberation is needed.
items.plain_english: One subjugates by sight alone; no consideration is needed in this matter.

items.question: Does the subjugating power fail even with mute or stone-like subjects?
premises: Mute, dull, and stone-like subjects are considered.
The verse asserts no exception.
The power is presented as unfailing.
items.inference: Even for the mute, dull, or stone-like, the result is not otherwise.
items.plain_english: Indeed, even for the mute, the dull, or one like stone, it is not otherwise.

items.question: Whom can the mantra practitioner bewilder through oblation?
premises: Oblation is performed by the mantra practitioner.
The effect is bewilderment.
The targets include dwellers of the three worlds.
items.inference: By oblation the mantra practitioner bewilders the dwellers of the three worlds.
items.plain_english: By oblation the mantra practitioner bewilders the dwellers of the three worlds.

rows.grounds: adds to the list of qualities

items.question: What qualities accompany the practitioner in these ritual attainments?
premises: Good fortune is attributed to the practitioner.
Charm and capability are also attributed.
The verse addresses a virtuous listener.
items.inference: The practitioner is endowed with good fortune, charm, and capability.
items.plain_english: O virtuous one, he is endowed with good fortune, charm, and capability.

items.question: What power over this world does the mantra practitioner obtain?
premises: The mantra practitioner obtains a great result.
The power to paralyze is stated.
This world is the object of that power.
items.inference: The mantra practitioner obtains greatness and can paralyze this world.
items.plain_english: The mantra practitioner obtains great power and should paralyze this world.

rows.grounds: compound listing groups whose women are targeted

items.question: Whose noble women can be brought under control by this ritual?
premises: Noble women of serpent-lords, asuras, and gods are named.
The ritual aims to bring them under control.
The action is enjoined.
items.inference: One should bring the noble women of serpent-lords, asuras, and gods under control.
items.plain_english: One should bring under control the noble women of serpent-lords, asuras, and gods.

rows.grounds: describes the kingdom as strongly defended

items.question: Can an entire well-fortified enemy kingdom be brought under one's control?
premises: An enemy kingdom with great fortresses is the target.
The entire kingdom is included.
The ritual aims to bring it under one’s own control.
items.inference: One should bring the entire well-fortified enemy kingdom under one’s own control.
items.plain_english: One should bring the entire, well-fortified enemy kingdom under one's own control.

items.question: What benefits arise for people through this ritual practice?
premises: Life, strength, health, and prosperity are listed.
These arise as results.
People are the recipients.
items.inference: Life, strength, health, and prosperity arise for people.
items.plain_english: Life, strength, health, and prosperity arise for people.

items.question: What gains result from an oblation of curd and honey?
premises: An oblation of curd and honey is performed.
Good fortune and wealth are desired results.
The attainment is enjoined.
items.inference: By an oblation of curd and honey one obtains good fortune and wealth.
items.plain_english: By an oblation of curd and honey one obtains good fortune and wealth.

rows.grounds: epithet of the practitioner or result

items.question: What powers over time, disease, and death are claimed without doubt?
premises: The practitioner is called destroyer of time, disease, and death.
These are presented as achieved powers.
Doubt is explicitly denied.
items.inference: He becomes a destroyer of time, disease, and death, without doubt.
items.plain_english: He becomes a destroyer of time, disease, and death; there is no doubt.

items.question: What immediate effect do red lotus oblations have on kings and the world?
premises: Red lotuses are used in oblation.
World-subjugation is the stated result.
Kings come under control instantly.
items.inference: With red lotuses one achieves world-subjugation and kings come under control instantly.
items.plain_english: With red lotuses comes subjugation of the world, and kings come under control in an instant.

rows.grounds: benefit attained, eloquence or power of speech

items.question: What benefits are obtained by oblation with white lotuses?
premises: White lotuses are offered in oblation.
Fortune and speech are named as attainments.
The verse addresses a beloved listener.
items.inference: By oblation with white lotuses one obtains fortune and speech.
items.plain_english: O beloved, by oblation with white lotuses one obtains fortune and speech.

items.question: What happens when the third hundred-thousand recitations are completed?
premises: The third hundred-thousand recitation is completed.
Celestial women appear as agents.
They act to bewilder the practitioner.
items.inference: When the third hundred-thousand recitations are completed, celestial women bewilder the practitioner.
items.plain_english: When the third hundred-thousand recitations are completed, celestial women cause bewilderment.

items.question: How must the practitioner remain when celestial women attempt to bewilder him?
premises: Celestial women indeed bewilder the practitioner.
This occurs in that stage of practice.
The practitioner is described as firm-minded.
items.inference: Though celestial women bewilder him there, he remains firm-minded.
items.plain_english: Indeed they bewilder the practitioner there, but he remains firm-minded.

items.question: What range of beings becomes submissive to the accomplished practitioner?
premises: Men and women are named as submissive.
The moving and unmoving are also included.
The verse addresses a beloved listener.
items.inference: Men, women, and even the moving and unmoving become submissive.
items.plain_english: O beloved, men, women, and even the moving and unmoving become submissive.

rows.grounds: describes the woman despite being drawn

items.question: Who comes to the practitioner under the bewildering power of the mantra?
premises: A chaste woman is described as coming.
She is bewildered by the mantra.
She comes properly to the practitioner.
items.inference: A chaste woman, bewildered by the mantra, comes properly to the practitioner.
items.plain_english: O beloved, a chaste woman, bewildered by the mantra, comes properly to the practitioner.
